title: Terraform for AWS
description: Learn how to manage AWS infrastructure with Terraform, including resources, variables, outputs, and remote state.

data.text: **Terraform** is an open-source infrastructure as code tool by HashiCorp. It uses a declarative configuration language called HCL (HashiCorp Configuration Language) and supports AWS through the AWS provider.

data.title: Core Concepts
items: **Provider** — a plugin that defines resources for a cloud provider (e.g., AWS)
**Variable** — input parameter that makes your configuration reusable
**Output** — value returned after Terraform applies (e.g., an IP address)

data.title: Terraform for AWS S3 Bucket (HCL)
data.content: This example creates an S3 bucket with versioning and server-side encryption.

data.text: Terraform state tracks which resources it manages. For teams, store state in a remote backend like **S3 + DynamoDB** for locking. This prevents multiple team members from modifying state at the same time.

terms.definition: HashiCorp Configuration Language — a declarative language for Terraform.
A Terraform plugin that enables management of a specific cloud or service.
Terraform's record of the resources it manages.
A shared location for state, such as S3, enabling team collaboration.

data.title: Important
data.text: Never store Terraform state locally in production. Always use a remote backend with state locking to prevent conflicts.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Terraform uses HCL to declare infrastructure as code
Variables make configurations reusable across environments
Remote backends enable team collaboration and state locking
